title: Karna: the wheel stuck, the death
hook: Karna appeals to the rules of war, and Krishna answers with questions
carry: he hangs his head in shame, and says nothing
tomorrow: Shalya: Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight

segments.voice: Yesterday, Karna's wheel sank into the earth and his weapon slipped from memory, two old curses at once. What wouldn't budge for you, and did you breathe before pulling? Day eight hundred forty-two.

Wait. That's what Karna calls out, standing on the ground with his hands on the wheel. Wait, Arjuna. A warrior in a chariot shouldn't strike a man who is on foot, whose wheel is stuck, who isn't ready. Those are the rules of fair fighting, he says, in effect. You know them. Remember dharma. Give me a moment to free the wheel. By the rules the armies agreed to, it sounds like a fair request, made by a man in real trouble. And it isn't Arjuna who answers. It's Krishna, from the driver's seat. Today, the answer, and the end of Karna.

Krishna's answer is a string of questions. Now you remember dharma, Karna? Where was it when Draupadi was dragged into the assembly hall and you mocked her? Where was it at the rigged game of dice? Where was it when young Abhimanyu was surrounded by many warriors at once and cut down? In Ganguli's English, Karna hears this, and he hangs his head in shame, and says nothing. He doesn't argue. He climbs back into the stuck chariot and fights on as well as he can. Then Arjuna, urged on by Krishna, takes up a single great arrow, and with it he cuts off Karna's head. Karna falls. And the epic gives one more picture. A light rises from Karna's fallen body and goes up into the sky, into the sun. Karna was, as the epic told it long before, a son of the sun god. Hold both halves of this man together, because the story does. The Karna who kept his promise to Kunti, and the Karna who laughed at Draupadi. The friend who never left Duryodhana, and the man who stood by while wrong was done. And one more thing. The Pandavas, cheering on the field, still don't know who just died. Kunti knows. Her sons will learn after the war that they have killed their eldest brother.
screen: `NOW YOU REMEMBER DHARMA?` · `KARNA HANGS HIS HEAD` · `THE LIGHT GOES TO THE SUN` · then, large: `A BROTHER THEY DIDN'T KNOW`

segments.voice: Sit still, and let your breath slow down. Let a question come to mind that you'd rather not be asked, one about something you did or didn't do. Don't build a defense. Don't explain. Just let the question be asked, and let the quiet after it stay quiet, the way Karna said nothing. Breathe in. Breathe out. Nothing to win here. If you pray, you can bring that question into your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Karna. The wheel stuck, the questions he couldn't answer, the light rising into the sun, and brothers who didn't yet know him.
Your line: he hangs his head in shame, and says nothing. Today, when you ask someone for fairness, remember once when you didn't give it. Day eight hundred forty-two.

howItsDone: Karna's death is retold in readings, regional theater, poems and serials, and Karna is discussed as a figure hard to judge: generous, loyal, wronged at birth, and complicit in wrong.

fork.setup: you're Krishna. Karna, on foot by his stuck wheel, asks Arjuna to wait, citing the rules of fair fighting. what do you say?
options: tell Arjuna to wait, as the rules require.
ask Karna where his dharma was when Draupadi was mocked and Abhimanyu cut down.
say nothing and let Arjuna decide.
fork.reveal: Krishna answers with questions about Draupadi, the dice game and Abhimanyu. Karna hangs his head and does not reply.

original.note: Karna: Kunti's firstborn son, raised in a charioteer's house, who died fighting his own brothers.

trapdoor: what you thought: Arjuna killed Karna unfairly while his wheel was stuck.
what it means: the epic lets Karna appeal to fairness and then has Krishna list the times he gave none.
what a scholar hears: the scene doesn't settle the question; some readers ask whether Krishna's answer justifies the blow, and the epic leaves it open.
recall: bites Nala and changes his shape

notes: Editor pass: replaced the practice (hold the good on the in-breath, the harm on the out-breath), which repeated days 827-828, with a silence practice tied to Karna's silence; 'the boy Abhimanyu' to 'young Abhimanyu'; softened 'readers still argue' and 'Hindus discuss'.
All paraphrase. Confirm the items in Krishna's list in Ganguli (Draupadi in the assembly, the dice game, Abhimanyu; the text may also mention the lac house and the exile); the script names three.
Confirm that Karna 'hung his head' and gave no answer, and that he fought on from the chariot before Arjuna's arrow (the Anjalika) beheaded him.
Confirm the light (energy) rising from Karna's body and entering the sun, as described in the Karna Parva.
The trapdoor's third floor now says 'some readers ask'; a Keeper may prefer to cut it.
Kunti's revelation is in the Stri Parva (and Yudhishthira's grief in the Shanti Parva); confirm.

Audit: the narrator no longer rules the request fair on its own authority ('it sounds like a fair request'), and the unsourced 'Arjuna hesitates' was cut. Keeper: the rules of fair fight are agreed in the Bhishma Parva; confirm the framing.
